subject: Science
chapter: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
source: Based on the uploaded Class 6 Curiosity Chapter 3 PDF (fecu103.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Original supplementary explanations and practice.
goals: Explain why food is needed for energy, growth, repair and normal body functions.
Describe a balanced diet in terms of variety and appropriate amounts.
Recognise that food habits vary across regions, families and cultures.
Explain the importance of hygiene, safe food handling and mindful eating.
Read a simple food record and identify patterns without judging people’s choices.
summary: Food supplies energy and nutrients needed for growth, repair and body functions. No single food supplies everything the body needs in the right amounts, so variety matters. Mindful eating includes noticing hunger and fullness, eating appropriate portions, choosing a varied diet when available, practising hygiene and respecting different food traditions. Individual dietary needs can vary with age, activity, health and culture.

concepts.title: Why we eat
concepts.explanation: Food provides energy and nutrients. Nutrients support growth, repair of tissues and processes such as maintaining body temperature. Water is also essential for transport and many body functions.
concepts.example: A child who is growing needs food that supplies energy as well as materials for building and repairing tissues.

concepts.title: Variety and balance
concepts.explanation: A balanced eating pattern includes a suitable variety of foods that together provide energy, protein, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water. Needs and available foods differ, so balance is about the overall pattern rather than one perfect meal.
concepts.example: A meal that includes a cereal or other energy source, pulses or another protein-rich food, vegetables and water may provide a wider range of nutrients than a meal containing only one food type.

concepts.title: Food diversity
concepts.explanation: Food choices are influenced by climate, crops, local ingredients, family traditions, religion, availability and personal needs. Different regions can have different healthy food patterns; one menu should not be assumed to fit everyone.
concepts.example: Rice-based, wheat-based, millet-based and other regional diets can all contribute to nourishment when the overall pattern supplies appropriate nutrients.

concepts.title: Mindful eating and portions
concepts.explanation: Mindful eating means paying attention to food, hunger, fullness, pace and the eating environment. Eating slowly and noticing fullness can help a person respond to their needs. It does not mean labelling foods or people as morally good or bad.
concepts.example: Pause during a meal and notice whether you are still hungry, rather than continuing only because food remains on the plate.

concepts.title: Hygiene and food safety
concepts.explanation: Wash hands before preparing or eating food, use clean utensils and safe water, store food appropriately and avoid food that appears spoiled. These practices reduce the risk of contamination and illness.
concepts.example: Covering cooked food and storing it at a suitable temperature helps protect it from insects and harmful microorganisms.

visual.title: A mindful food routine
steps: Wash hands and use clean utensils

workedExamples.question: A student records eating only one kind of food at most meals. What can the student investigate to understand the pattern?
steps: Record meals over several days without changing the record to look better.
Identify the main food groups and variety present across the whole period.
Compare the pattern with age-appropriate balanced-diet guidance from a reliable source or teacher.
Discuss practical changes with a trusted adult, considering availability, allergies, culture and individual needs.
workedExamples.answer: Use a food record to notice variety and gaps, then seek appropriate guidance rather than making a diagnosis from one meal.

workedExamples.question: Why is handwashing relevant even when food looks clean?
steps: Microorganisms and dirt may not be visible.
Hands can transfer contamination to food or utensils.
Washing with soap and clean water reduces this transfer.
workedExamples.answer: Food can look clean while still being contaminated; handwashing reduces the chance of transferring germs.

practice.question: Name three reasons the body needs food.
practice.answer: Energy, growth and repair; food also supplies nutrients needed for body functions.
practice.why: Food supports several different needs, not only hunger.

practice.question: Why is variety important in a diet?
practice.answer: Different foods provide different nutrients, so a varied overall pattern makes it easier to meet the body’s needs.
practice.why: No single food normally supplies every nutrient in appropriate amounts.

practice.question: Give two safe food-handling practices.
practice.answer: Wash hands, use clean utensils and safe water, cover food, and store it appropriately.

practice.question: Why should food traditions be discussed respectfully?
practice.answer: Food choices reflect culture, region, access and individual needs; respectful discussion avoids unfair assumptions about people’s diets.
practice.why: A healthy overall pattern can take different forms in different settings.

mcqs.why: Food supplies energy and nutrients for body functions, growth and repair.

mcqs.q: A balanced eating pattern is best understood as…
options: variety and suitable amounts across the overall diet
mcqs.why: Balance concerns the combination and amounts of foods over time, with individual needs considered.

options: to reduce transfer of germs and contamination

mcqs.why: Mindfulness involves attention to the eating experience and body signals.

mcqs.q: Food patterns differ across regions partly because of…
mcqs.why: Local ingredients, climate, availability and traditions influence diets.

revision: Food supplies energy and nutrients for growth, repair and body functions.
A varied overall diet helps provide different nutrients; needs differ between people.
Food patterns reflect regional ingredients, culture, availability and individual needs.
Mindful eating means noticing hunger, fullness, pace and the eating environment.
Handwashing, clean utensils, safe water and proper storage support food safety.

chapterTest.instructions: Answer using practical examples. Avoid judging diets without considering needs and context.

questions.q: Explain why the body needs a variety of foods.
questions.answer: Different foods provide different nutrients; variety helps supply energy, protein, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water in suitable amounts.

questions.q: Describe three steps that support food hygiene.
questions.answer: Wash hands with soap and clean water, use clean utensils and safe water, and cover/store food appropriately.
Paying attention to food, pace, hunger and fullness, and responding thoughtfully to one’s needs.

questions.q: Why should a food record cover more than one meal?
questions.answer: A longer record shows patterns and variety over time; one meal may not represent the whole diet.
